title: Segmented analytics endpoint authorization middleware and auditable role mapping
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Analytics endpoints and usage views expose aggregated and per-token usage data. Currently access checks are coarse (org-level allowlists) and implemented inconsistently across services, leading to audit gaps and noisy incident reports when a customer expected more restricted visibility.

Goal: Implement a single, testable authorization middleware for console analytics endpoints that enforces per-route RBAC, supports attribute-based policies (org_id, billing_role, scim_groups, product_tier), emits auditable logs, and produces decisions that downstream data pipelines can use to apply column-level scoping or row-level filters. The middleware must be performant (target added latency < 6ms p95), cacheable, and compatible with the entitlement syncer and our existing session tokens.

Scope:
- HTTP/gRPC middleware used by console backend services that serve usage/analytics views (per-route enforcement).
- Policy model: route -> required permissions OR attribute expression (e.g., org_id == request.org && role in [owner, analyst]).
- Integration points: entitlement-syncer (group/role sync), SCIM/SSO group mapping, metrics pipeline (tag decisions), audit log sink (Kinesis->S3) for compliance.
- Downstream hinting: return decision headers that analytics ingestion can use to apply query scoping on incremental pipelines.

Out of scope for this ticket: rewriting the full query engine to enforce column-level encryption; that will be a follow-up.

Proposal summary:
1) Add a lightweight AuthorizationService plus in-process middleware. The service exposes a cached Evaluate(permission_key, attributes) endpoint.
2) Implement policy files per-service (YAML) with explicit route bindings and fallback policies.
3) Cache decisions keyed by hashed (org_id, route, requester_roles) for 60s with early invalidation on entitlement-syncer notifications.
4) Emit structured audit entries for every allow/deny decision to the existing audit log pipeline.
5) Provide a header X-Analytics-Auth-Decision with a signed token that downstream pipelines can consume to apply query scoping in ETL jobs.

Non-functional constraints: low latency, safe defaults (deny on error), observability (decision distribution, cache hit rate), and feature flags for gradual rollout.
comments: 2026-02-11 Maya Patel: RFC posted to docs.redwood.ai/console/rfc/analytics-auth. High-level design approved by PM and Security for prototyping.

2026-02-18 Lucas Rivera: Spike completed for in-process middleware. Measured cold Evaluate RPC = 12ms; with local LRU cache hit p95 = 3.8ms. Recorded benchmark results in /docs/benchmarks/analytics-auth-2026-02-18.md.
2026-02-24 Security Review: initial findings indicate need for signed audit payloads and HMAC key rotation support. Added security_review_required flag and linked KMS ticket.
2026-03-01 PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4828 implementing middleware and basic policy loader. Review feedback requested from @security and @data-platform.

2026-03-05 QA: added integration tests that simulate mixed-role orgs and assert both allow/deny and emitted audit events. Found race where entitlement-syncer update led to stale cache for 60s; added notification hook to invalidate keys.
2026-03-10 Lucas Rivera: Preparing canary rollout. Feature flag console.auth.analytics.enabled created. Draft rollback runbook linked.
acceptance_criteria: All protected analytics endpoints return 403 for requests that lack the required permission according to the YAML policy bindings.
Audit log emitted for every allow and deny decision with fields: timestamp, org_id, route, requester_id, decision, policy_id, request_id.
Cache hit rate > 70% under a synthetic workload that mirrors production traffic (see benchmark doc) and added latency <= 6ms p95 for cached decisions.
Downstream pipelines can consume X-Analytics-Auth-Decision header and apply row-level scoping based on the signed decision token.
Rollout behind feature flag with automated canary that compares query costs and error rates between control and canary for 48 hours.
Security review completed and KMS/HSM keys in place for signing audit tokens.
implementation_steps: Add AuthorizationService interface and in-process middleware to console backend services.
Implement policy YAML loader and basic language for attribute expressions.
Integrate with entitlement-syncer to receive role/group updates and invalidation events.
Emit structured audit events to the existing audit pipeline and add dashboards for decision counts and deny reasons.
Expose X-Analytics-Auth-Decision header with short-lived signed token for downstream consumption.
Add e2e tests + performance benchmarks and run load tests against staging analytics traffic.
Perform security review and enable KMS key rotation for signing keys.
Canary rollout: 5% orgs for 24h, then 25% for 24h, then 100% if metrics are within thresholds.
Post-rollout: add per-route telemetry and tidy policy files.
Document migration guide for product teams and update Console docs.
rollout_plan: Feature flag enabled: console.auth.analytics.enabled = false by default.
Stage 1: internal-only canary with admin orgs for smoke validation (2 days). Monitor audit volume and latency.
Stage 2: 5% external orgs. Compare resource usage and query result parity (allow/deny) vs baseline.
Stage 3: 25% external orgs. Validate entitlement-syncer notifications clear stale cache; watch for 403 regression tickets.
Stage 4: All orgs. Ramp KMS key rotation and perform an end-to-end audit export to S3 for regulatory teams.
Rollback criteria: >0.5% increase in error rate for protected endpoints, or p95 added latency > 12ms, or audit pipeline lag > 5 minutes.
notes: Trade-offs: In-process caching keeps latency low but requires reliable invalidation; using an external PDP (policy decision point) would centralize policy but add network hops. We chose hybrid: cached local decisions with an external admin API for policy changes.
Performance mitigation: batch Evaluate calls for multi-route UI fetches to avoid N separate policy checks for a single page load.
Data pipeline integration: analytics ingestion will use the signed header to add a scoped flag to events so that pre-aggregation jobs can drop columns not visible to the requester.
Testing notes: add chaos test to simulate entitlement-syncer outage and assert deny-on-error behavior (fail-closed).
Future work: column-level access controls, finer-grained masking for PII in usage payloads, and a policy authoring UI in Console.
